text:
samir: hey all 44b. first day! i'm on NixOS (22.11) on a ThinkPad and following the repo bootstrap. hitting weird stuff: `asdf install` fails because the build tools aren't found, `./bootstrap.sh` assumes direnv but we use home-manager, and bootstrap wants .envrc/.env.local which feels off on Nix. also ssh-agent integration with key in gpg is confusing. who's best to ping?

fiona: welcome Samir! NixOS is a bit different. we usually prefer using nix to provide build deps rather than installing system packages. check if repo has a `shell.nix` or `default.nix` that sets the buildInputs. run `nix develop` (flakes: `nix develop .#devShell`) — that will give the env with compilers and headers for asdf builds.

samir: ah we do have `flake.nix` and `shell.nix` in the repo, but i wasn't sure how to use flakes. i ran `asdf install` outside of nix and it couldn't find `gcc`/`pkg-config`.

marc: if you're on NixOS, do your asdf builds inside the nix shell so the native headers are visible. e.g.:

```
# with flakes enabled
nix develop .#devShell
# inside the shell
asdf install
```

That avoids global changes. We also have a dev script `scripts/nix-asdf` that wraps asdf commands under the right nix env.

samir: nice — `nix develop` allowed asdf to find gcc and pkg-config. thanks. question about dotfiles/home-manager: the bootstrap.sh assumes `direnv` and sources `.envrc`. I manage dotfiles with home-manager, and direnv is configured via home-manager modules. Should I still create `.envrc` or is there a preferred Nix-y flow?

fiona: prefer a Nix-y flow: create an `overlays` entry in your home-manager or add a `programs.direnv.enable = true` and then add `.envrc` to the repo root with `use flake` or `use nix`. Example `.envrc`: `use flake` or `use nix` will enter the flake dev environment automatically. If bootstrap expects plain `export` style `.envrc`, add a tiny shim that sources `.env.local` after the nix directives.

samir: example `.envrc`?

marc: something minimal like:

```
# .envrc
use flake
export $(cat .env.local | xargs)
```

But keep secrets out of git — copy `env.example` to `.env.local` with placeholders as usual.

samir: got it. SSH/GPG question: i have a key in my `gpg` keyring and use `gpg-agent` for ssh. VS Code (native) can't see the gpg ssh socket; home-manager sets `ssh-agent` differently. any tips?

ryn: on NixOS with home-manager we usually enable `home-manager.users.<you>.programs.gpg-agent.enable = true` and `programs.gpg-agent.extraConfig = ''enable-ssh-support'';` in your home.nix. Then ensure your shell rc has:

```
export SSH_AUTH_SOCK=$(gpgconf --list-dirs agent-ssh-socket)
export GPG_TTY=$(tty)
```

Also for VS Code, add `remote.SSH.forwardAgent` if using Remote - SSH. If you denied a keychain prompt earlier, restart the app so it re-prompts.

samir: i do use home-manager but hadn't enabled gpg-agent ssh support. enabling that and `gpgconf --launch gpg-agent` made ssh-add `-l` show my key. thanks.

fiona: one Nix-specific gotcha: don't run `sudo apt install` or try to mutate the system; package management is declarative. use `nix-env -iA` for per-user installs or add to your `configuration.nix`/home-manager if it's something system-wide.

samir: noted. last quickchecks before i ping eng for CI run?

marc: run `nix develop .#devShell` then inside it: `make ci-local` (fast) and `scripts/check-env`. we have a `scripts/check-nix` that ensures flakes and home-manager are configured; run that too. If everything passes, open a PR and tag your onboarding buddy.

infra-bot: [onboarding] Samir's onboarding ticket created. infra will verify your Nix configuration for VPN keys and 1Password access.

samir: awesome, i'm unblocked. i'll add Nix-specific notes to my onboarding doc for future NixOS folks. thanks everyone!
